set_rules.rule: Composed tasks: cluster_id = compose.cluster_id(compose.signature(reference)) ('chain:' + v2 signature); build.py asserts compose.signature_split(compose.signature(ref)) == SPLIT (v2, not v1) and prints the v2 signature of the start graph, the reference and every variant. A variant may have a different signature only if it is a genuine structural alternative; list it in task.json notes so the reserved list can include it. Never reach a split by adding plumbing, swapping ids or reordering ports; if a design flips split under a natural alternative, change the function. Seed-derived tasks keep the seed file and seed split; their cluster_id stays the seed path.

Fixers do not edit handoff/training_team/flowgraph_reserved_signatures.txt. After all groups finish, one final step regenerates it from compose.audit_items over the fixed items (old signatures of re-themed tasks are released, new ones reserved).

Under the 16 Oct decision every instruction is a user's request to GRC-Agent about the open flowgraph. Build tasks: the open flowgraph is empty except for a samp_rate variable, so the instruction asks to build in it and states the sample rate to use (e.g. 'set the sample rate to 48 kHz'); do not say 'Build a GNU Radio flowgraph' as if starting a new file. Modify/repair/tune: refer to 'this flowgraph' and its blocks by what they do (names visible in inspect_graph may be used). Never mention .grc/YAML, files of the flowgraph itself, benchmarks, oracles, gates or canaries. start_grc stays null for build tasks in this stage (gates.py treats build as 'no starting flowgraph'); the empty start graph and golden_calls.json come with the edit-format conversion stage.

Every requirement the instruction states is checked by V6 and nothing unstated is required. State tolerances in the instruction (frequency within 1 %, amplitude/RMS within 5 %, etc.) and the measurement window ('after the first N samples' / 'from 0.1 s on'). Thresholds come from the stated spec (computed from the stated numbers or from the reference taps), never from run-to-run noise alone; an idealised expectation that real correct designs miss by > half the tolerance must be recomputed (cf. test-15 F2). Where the structure is the point (e.g. 'rectify', 'phase-locked loop', 'phasing method', 'keep the mixer'), add graph_checks (path / block_present) that accept every block that legitimately does the job; otherwise phrase behaviourally. Every 'keep X unchanged' clause is either checked (p2p signal check, edge observation point or graph check) or removed.

Any task whose observation needs more items than a short run gives says so with the set sentence: 'The flowgraph should keep producing samples until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples.' Record it in spec_properties as a run condition checked by V5 liveness (at least n_items at every observation point); do not claim more. Drop phrases that invite fixed-length files ('so every run writes the same samples').

modify = the user asks for a new function or a structural change (blocks added, removed or rewired; behaviour the start graph cannot produce by values alone). parameter-tune = the user states a target behaviour reachable by changing parameter values only; the instruction says 'change parameter values only; do not add, remove or rewire blocks' and the oracle enforces it with graph_checks same_blocks_as_start (group p2p) plus the connection check from tooling T1 once available. Tune variants must obey the same rule (no extra or deleted variables unless the instruction allows it). repair = the start is broken (fault injected) and the instruction gives intended behaviour plus the visible symptom only.

Proposed rule for the team (pending): L1 = at most 5 functional blocks (graph_checks.max_functional_blocks counting: everything except options/variables, sinks included), single rate, no modulator+demodulator chain; a single filtering stage does not by itself make an item L2. L2 = 6-15 functional blocks or any rate change or modulation/demodulation. Message ports, tags, PDUs, OFDM, Embedded Python -> L3 (proposal 5.2). Re-themed L1 items must respect the 5-block budget (use edge observation points, which add no block, instead of extra File Sinks when the budget is tight).

For repair starts that fail before V6 (V2/V3), p2p means 'properties carried by parts of the graph the fault does not touch'; every check whose value depends on the repaired element is f2p. Say so once in spec_properties (checked_by text). Where cheap, prove the p2p group on the start with the faulted branch parked (test-09 F4).

Every observation point names the File Sink by file name AND item type in the instruction, and the point's sink params include 'type' so a wrongly typed sink fails. Prefer a second observation point (input tap or edge point) whenever an output-only oracle can be satisfied by a shortcut generator; then add a p2p check on it.

>= 5 distinct, valid, spec-breaking mutants with correct 'breaks' labels; no two mutants with the same faulty behaviour; at least one near-miss on every stated number that matters; a mutant for every stated 'keep' requirement; documented survivors must be in the set (kill rate still >= 90 %). >= 2 genuinely different correct variants, each obeying the instruction literally; add every valid alternative a reviewer showed (or explain in notes why it is invalid under the new wording).

Known oracle limits go into review.notes (the team sheet shows it), not only authoring_notes. disjointness names the nearest training-side specs (reports/reference/training_task_specs.json) and says why the task differs. Seed-derived tasks record every conversion change in perturbation.changes (incl. stripped author/copyright options and widget->variable conversions) and keep the GPL attribution in notes (licence decision is the team's).

oracles.band_fraction changed on 18 Oct (real one-sided spectra now count non-DC bins twice). Every task with band_fraction checks on real signals, especially with DC or Nyquist content, must re-derive its thresholds from the stated spec with the corrected oracle and re-run gates; new themes must be calibrated with it from the start.

Fixers edit only their task directories (and nothing in data/, the documents or ~/grc-agent). They do not edit src/ or tests/. If a fix needs a tool feature from the tooling list, use it once it exists; until then implement the best fix possible with existing features and list the remaining gap in review.notes and in the fixer's report.

Each fixer rebuilds through build.py (taskio.save) and re-runs './gb tier-f gates <task_dir>' until passed; gates.json must be current. Tasks with more than one observation point are re-gated again after tooling T7.

gbf-dev-01.new_theme: BUILD L1 (dev) - frame-sync word detector on a bit stream. In the empty flowgraph (samp_rate only; the rate is irrelevant to the output, state e.g. 32 kHz), the user asks for: a repeating Vector Source of unpacked bits (bytes 0/1, an explicit list of about 64-96 bits stated in the instruction) that contains one copy of a 16-bit sync word per period (choose a non-standard word, not CCSDS 0x1ACFFC1D, e.g. 1110 1011 0010 0001) and one near-miss copy with exactly one bit wrong; a detector that marks every error-free occurrence (no bit errors allowed) - GNU Radio's Correlate Access Code - Bit (digital_correlate_access_code_bb, threshold 0) outputs one byte per input bit with the data bit in bit 0 and a flag (+2) on the bit that follows the last bit of the sync word; write that byte stream to a File Sink flags.dat, item type byte. State the required output encoding behaviourally (one byte per input bit = the bit value, plus 2 on the first bit after each complete error-free sync word; the near-miss copy is not marked). Observation: flags.dat (byte). Oracle: equal_prefix exact over >= 3 periods (max_offset 0; the first marker cannot occur before bit 16), mean as a secondary check. Graph check path from blocks_vector_source_x to blocks_file_sink via a detector (digital_correlate_access_code_bb, digital_correlate_access_code_tag_xx with a tag-to-flag stage, or an FIR correlator + threshold) because a hard-coded Vector Source holding the expected output would otherwise pass. Mutants: threshold 1 (marks the near-miss), sync word with one bit flipped or reversed, output of the raw bits (detector bypassed), byte vs float type, marker on the last sync bit (off by one). Verified v2: data_source|frame_sync -> dev (also with the tag variant). FIR-correlator+threshold alternative would be data_source|filter|nonlinear (dev; no task uses it). Training specs: nothing on access codes (t18 PSK31 monitor decodes symbols, different).

gbf-dev-02.new_theme: BUILD L1 (dev) - Rayleigh flat-fading envelope. In the empty flowgraph the user asks to simulate the amplitude of a Rayleigh-fading channel gain: complex Gaussian noise with RMS magnitude 0.8 (state the meaning: sqrt(mean |z|^2) = 0.8; GNU Radio's complex Noise Source with amplitude 0.8 does this - fixer verifies), its magnitude written as float to envelope.dat, sample rate 48 kHz. Requirements stated with tolerances: mean envelope 0.8*sqrt(pi)/2 = 0.709 (within 2 %), RMS 0.8 (within 2 %), so mean/RMS = 0.886 (a half-normal |real noise| gives 0.798, a constant gives 1); optionally the fraction below the median is not checkable - do not state it. Observation: envelope.dat (float), n >= 65536 after a short skip; run sentence (R5). Oracle: mean and rms (calibrate over 10 seeds; noise seed is free, so do not require one). No graph check needed (behavioural: any structure producing a Rayleigh envelope of that RMS passes). Alternatives: Fast Noise Source; two real noise sources (RMS 0.8/sqrt2 each) + Float To Complex + Complex To Mag (both envelope|noise); Complex To Mag^2 + sqrt (Transcendental) -> envelope|noise|nonlinear (train: list it so it is reserved). Mutants: Complex To Mag^2 without sqrt, |real noise| (Abs of float noise), amplitude 1.6, uniform noise, Complex To Real instead of magnitude. Verified v2: envelope|noise -> dev. Training: t08_run_verify_probe (noise to file + level probe) is the nearest spec; differs (envelope statistics of complex noise, no probe, no level-vs-theory report) - say so in disjointness.

gbf-dev-03.new_theme: MODIFY L1 (dev) - add a matched filter to an NRZ stream. Start graph: samp_rate 32000; a repeating Vector Source (float) holding a rectangular NRZ test pattern of +-1 symbols at 8 samples per symbol (4 kBd; about 16-32 symbols, written as an explicit expression of symbols repeated 8 times), connected to a File Sink nrz.dat (float). The user asks to add a matched filter for these rectangular pulses: integrate (sum) over one symbol length and scale so a full symbol gives +-1, at the same sample rate (one output per input sample, no decimation), written to a new File Sink mf.dat (float), leaving nrz.dat unchanged. Expected mf.dat: triangular ramps reaching exactly +-1 at each symbol end (values are multiples of 1/8, exact in float). Oracle: f2p equal_prefix on mf.dat against the reference output from sample 0 (verify Moving Average and FIR [1/8]*8 give bit-identical samples; if not, use corr_ref >= 0.9999 with max_lag 0 plus max_abs 1.0), p2p equal_prefix on nrz.dat. Graph check (structure is the point and a hard-coded Vector Source would pass): path blocks_vector_source_x -> {blocks_moving_average_xx, fir_filter_xxx, fft_filter_xxx} -> blocks_file_sink (only blocks that can realise the rectangular matched filter exactly). Variants: Moving Average (length 8, scale 1/8), FIR filter taps [0.125]*8, FFT filter. Mutants: length 7 and 16, scale 1 (peaks +-8), filter bypassed, filter fed from a delayed/other branch, decimating integrate-and-dump (wrong rate), nrz.dat changed. Verified v2: start data_source (train, irrelevant), reference data_source|filter -> dev (moving average and FIR alike). Note: an Integrate-and-dump with decimation would be data_source|filter|resample - excluded by the 'same sample rate' requirement. Training: t19_rssi_meter_build uses a moving average for level metering - different purpose; record.

gbf-dev-04.new_theme: REPAIR L1 (dev, fault undefined_variable, expected V3) - heterodyne mixer to an IF. Graph (fs 48 kHz, float): RF test carrier Signal Source 10.7 kHz amplitude 0.8 (block name e.g. 'rf') and a local-oscillator Signal Source (amplitude 1) whose frequency is the variable lo_freq, a Multiply, a Low Pass Filter (cutoff 4 kHz, width 1 kHz) and a File Sink if.dat (float). Fault: the variable block lo_freq (8.7 kHz) is deleted while the LO still refers to it -> 'name lo_freq is not defined' at V3. Instruction: intended behaviour only - the RF carrier must come out of if.dat as a 2 kHz IF tone with amplitude 0.4 (half the RF amplitude, as for an ideal multiplier with a unit LO), within 1 % / 5 %, with the mixer's sum product removed (>= 40 dB down), RF source unchanged; symptom = GRC refuses to generate because a parameter value cannot be evaluated. Do not say which side the LO is on: LO 8.7 kHz and 12.7 kHz both give a 2 kHz IF and both are correct (make them two variants). Observation: if.dat (float) plus an edge observation point on the RF source output (no extra block; keeps the 5-block budget) with p2p checks (10.7 kHz, RMS 0.566). Graph check (p2p): path analog_sig_source_x -> {blocks_multiply_xx, blocks_multiply_ff} -> low-pass-type filter -> blocks_file_sink, so deleting the mixer and writing a 2 kHz tone fails. Oracle: peak_freq 2000 +-20, rms 0.283 +-5 %, band_fraction 1.9-2.1 kHz >= 0.9999 after the filter settles. Mutants: lo_freq 9.7 kHz (IF 1 kHz), LPF bypassed (sum product present), LPF cutoff 1.5 kHz (IF attenuated), LO amplitude 0.5, Multiply replaced by Add (no mixing), LO samp_rate 32 kHz (rate error), RF changed (p2p). Verified v2: filter|mix|tone -> dev with either port order. Training: Qoherent spec 06_query_knowledge_multiply ('multiply the two sine tones instead of adding them') is the nearest - this task is a repair of an undefined LO variable with an IF target and filter; record it in disjointness.

gbf-dev-05.new_theme: PARAMETER-TUNE L1 (dev) - Gaussian noise limiter (amplifier saturation model). Start graph (fs 48 kHz, float): Noise Source, Gaussian, amplitude 0.5 (state as RMS/standard deviation 0.5), -> Rail (analog_rail_ff, lo -1.5, hi 1.5) -> File Sink limited.dat. User target: 'the noise feeding the limiter should now have a standard deviation of 0.4, and the limiter must clip symmetrically so that exactly the loudest 5 % of samples are clipped (2.5 % at each end)'. The model must work out the clip level 1.96 * 0.4 = 0.784 (Gaussian 97.5 % quantile) and set amp 0.4, lo -0.784, hi 0.784; values only (R6). Oracle: max_abs 0.784 within 1 % (the largest sample equals the clip level once clipping occurs), min (tooling T4) -0.784 within 1 % or a mean check for symmetry, rms of the clipped Gaussian computed from the stated numbers (fixer derives E[min(x^2, c^2)] analytically and checks over seeds; the band of 1 % around 1.96 sigma must separate 1.645 sigma and 2.576 sigma clips), graph_checks same_blocks_as_start (+T1 connections) group p2p. Mutants: clip at 1.645 sigma (10 %), at 2.576 sigma (1 %), asymmetric limits, sigma left at 0.5, Rail bypassed, clip levels computed for sigma 0.5. Verified v2: noise|nonlinear -> dev. Training: no limiter/clipping spec.

gbf-dev-06.new_theme: BUILD L2 (dev) - upper-sideband SSB transmitter by the phasing method. In the empty flowgraph the user asks for: a two-tone audio test signal at an audio rate of 8 kHz (float cosines 700 Hz amplitude 0.4 and 1.9 kHz amplitude 0.25, summed; avoid dial-tone frequencies), interpolated to 48 kHz, turned into an analytic signal with a Hilbert transformer, shifted up by a 10 kHz complex carrier and reduced to its real part: a real USB signal at 48 kHz with tones at 10.7 kHz (0.4) and 11.9 kHz (0.25); lower sideband (9.3 and 8.1 kHz) and carrier each >= 30 dB below the weaker wanted tone (calibrate the Hilbert length the instruction allows). Outputs: audio.dat (float, 8 kHz, the summed audio) and ssb.dat (float, 48 kHz). Structural wording ('phasing method with a Hilbert transformer') -> graph_checks: block_present hilbert_fc (min 1) and path audio source -> hilbert_fc -> blocks_file_sink(ssb.dat); this is required, because the filter method or a Weaver modulator gives combine|filter|mix|resample|tone, which is gbf-test-18's test cell. Oracle: on ssb.dat band_fraction around 10.7 and 11.9 kHz with the stated amplitude ratio, LSB bands and carrier band <= the stated level, rms, after a skip for filter start-up; on audio.dat peak 700 Hz at fs 8000 and rms. Run sentence (R5); tolerances stated. Variants: Rational Resampler + Hilbert + Multiply with complex LO + Complex To Real; Interpolating FIR (low-pass taps) + Hilbert + Rotator; Repeat + low-pass + Hilbert. Mutants: LSB (LO -10 kHz or conjugate), Hilbert removed (DSB), Hilbert 9 taps (poor suppression), carrier 9.5 kHz, interpolation 4 (wrong output rate), audio tone amplitude swap. Verified v2: combine|filter|hilbert|mix|resample|tone -> dev (with Multiply+LO or Rotator, resampler or interpolating FIR). Generating the audio directly at 48 kHz gives combine|hilbert|mix|tone (test) - excluded because the instruction fixes the 8 kHz audio rate and audio.dat checks it. Training: none (no SSB spec).

gbf-test-01.new_theme: BUILD L1 (test) - full-wave rectifier of a mains-like waveform. In the empty flowgraph: sample rate 48 kHz; a 50 Hz cosine (float) of peak amplitude 2.0; its full-wave rectified version (output = |input|) written as float to rectified.dat. Requirements stated with tolerances: average 2*2/pi = 1.273 (within 2 %), RMS 2/sqrt2 = 1.414 (within 2 %), largest value 2.0 (within 2 %), never negative, strongest AC component at 100 Hz (twice the mains frequency, within 1 %). Observation: rectified.dat (float), n = 48000 after a short skip (1 Hz bins; run sentence R5). Oracle: mean, rms, max_abs, min (T4) >= -0.01 if available, band_fraction 90-110 Hz ~ 16/(9 pi^2) = 0.180 of the power and 190-210 Hz ~ 0.0072 (derive with the corrected band_fraction, R12), peak_freq of the AC part (check whether peak_freq skips DC; else use band checks only). Graph check: path analog_sig_source_x -> {blocks_abs_xx, blocks_complex_to_mag, blocks_complex_to_mag_squared + blocks_transcendental sqrt, blocks_max_xx} -> blocks_file_sink, because a Vector Source holding one period of |cos| would otherwise pass. Variants: Abs (float); Float To Complex + Complex To Mag; Complex To Mag^2 + sqrt. Mutants: half-wave rectifier (Rail lo 0: average 0.637), squared instead of abs (average 2.0), amplitude 1, 60 Hz, abs bypassed (average 0), offset added, samp_rate 32 kHz. Verified v2: envelope|tone -> test (Abs and F2C+Mag alike; the input-tap variant too). Training: none.

gbf-test-02.new_theme: BUILD L1 (test) - carrier recovery with a phase-locked loop. In the empty flowgraph: sample rate 32 kHz; a received carrier simulated as a complex tone at +2.4 kHz, amplitude 1, plus complex Gaussian noise of amplitude 0.7 (SNR about 3 dB) added to it; a phase-locked loop that locks to the carrier and outputs a clean unit-amplitude reference carrier (analog_pll_refout_cc; the instruction states the lock range in Hz, e.g. +-4 kHz, which the model converts to rad/sample, and leaves the loop bandwidth to the model), written as complex to carrier.dat. Requirements (after 0.25 s of settling, stated): RMS 1.0 within 2 %, no sample above 1.05 in magnitude (constant envelope), at least 99 % of the power within 25 Hz of +2.4 kHz (calibrate against loop bandwidths that a competent engineer would pick, and against noisy/unlocked designs). Observation: carrier.dat (complex). Structural wording ('phase-locked loop', 'recover the carrier from the noisy signal') -> graph check path from the noise source through a carrier-tracking block {analog_pll_refout_cc, digital_costas_loop_cc, digital_fll_band_edge_cc? only if it outputs a clean carrier - verify} to blocks_file_sink; this rules out writing a clean 2.4 kHz tone directly. Variants: PLL Ref Out; Costas loop order 2 output (verify it behaves as a carrier reference on an unmodulated carrier; otherwise drop); different loop bandwidths. Mutants: PLL bypassed (noisy output fails purity), lock range not containing 2.4 kHz (no lock), carrier at 2.8 kHz, noise amplitude 3 (no lock at that bandwidth, if it really fails), output taken before the PLL, PLL Carrier Tracking (outputs the de-rotated input, near 0 Hz). Block budget: 5 (tone, noise, add, PLL, sink) - no extra sink. Verified v2: carrier_sync|combine|noise|tone -> test (PLL Ref Out and Costas alike). Training: none on PLLs.

gbf-test-05.new_theme: BUILD L1 (test) - BPSK hard-decision demapper with bit packing. In the empty flowgraph the user provides a receiver's soft decisions as a repeating Vector Source of 32 float values listed in the instruction (noisy +-1 values, a few close to 0, one exactly 0.0) and asks for hard decisions with the convention bit 0 for a positive soft value and bit 1 for a negative one (0.0 decides to 0), packed 8 bits per byte, most significant bit first, written to bits.dat with item type byte (4 bytes per period). The model must know that GNU Radio's Binary Slicer maps x >= 0 to 1 (so the polarity must be inverted) and how to pack bits (Unpacked To Packed / Pack K Bits, MSB first). Observation: bits.dat (byte). Oracle: equal_prefix exact over >= 4 periods, max_offset 0; mean as a secondary check. Graph check: path blocks_vector_source_x -> {digital_binary_slicer_fb, blocks_threshold_ff, digital_constellation_decoder_cb, blocks_float_to_char/uchar...} -> blocks_file_sink, because a Vector Source holding the 4 expected bytes would otherwise pass (record the remaining limit per team_decisions). Variants: Multiply Const -1 + Binary Slicer + Pack K Bits; Threshold (lo=hi=0, output 0/1 float) + inversion + Float To UChar + Pack; Constellation Decoder with a BPSK object whose point 0 is +1. Mutants: polarity not inverted, LSB-first packing, unpacked output (one bit per byte), decision threshold 0.5, 0.0 decided as 1, float output type. Verified v2: data_source|linear_demod -> test (slicer, slicer+invert, constellation decoder); Threshold alternative data_source|nonlinear (test); Float To Char alternative data_source|quantize (dev; no dev task uses it). Training: t02_qpsk_ber_chain includes decoding inside a QPSK BER chain; this item is BPSK demapping + packing only - record.

gbf-test-07.new_theme: MODIFY L1 (test) - align a reference stream with a FIR filter's output (group-delay compensation). Start graph (fs 48 kHz, float): a Signal Source cosine 1.5 kHz amplitude 0.8 feeds (a) an FIR Filter (fir_filter_xxx, fff) whose taps are a literal list of 41 symmetric low-pass taps held in a taps variable (literal so the model can count them; e.g. the rounded values of firdes.low_pass(1, 48000, 3000, 1000) truncated/redesigned to 41 taps) -> File Sink out.dat, and (b) directly a File Sink ref.dat. The user: 'ref.dat and out.dat are misaligned on my scope by the filter's delay; delay the stream written to ref.dat by exactly the filter's group delay so that they line up; leave out.dat unchanged'. The model must know that a linear-phase FIR with N taps delays by (N-1)/2 = 20 samples and insert a Delay of 20 (ref.dat then starts with 20 zeros). Oracle: f2p equal_prefix on ref.dat from sample 0 against the reference output (20 zeros, then the cosine; exact floats), p2p equal_prefix/corr_ref on out.dat unchanged. The zero prefix pins the delay exactly (a second phase-shifted oscillator, or a delay of 20 + 32k, fails). Variants: Delay block 20; pure-delay FIR [0]*20+[1] (bit-identical); delay given as an expression (len(taps)-1)//2. Mutants: delay 19, 21, 41 (N), 52 (one period later), delay placed on the out.dat branch, no delay, filter taps changed (p2p), tone changed (p2p). Block budget 5 (source, FIR, Delay, 2 sinks). Verified v2: start filter|tone, reference delay|filter|tone -> test. The pure-delay-FIR variant is filter|tone (gbf-test-10's cell, same split, different function) - list it in notes as an alternative link. Training: none on group delay.

gbf-test-08.new_theme: REPAIR L1 (test, fault deleted_connection, expected V3) - phase comparator between two oscillators. Graph (fs 48 kHz): reference oscillator = complex Signal Source 1 kHz amplitude 1; test oscillator = complex Signal Source 1.005 kHz amplitude 1; Multiply Conjugate (test x conj(reference)) -> Complex To Arg -> File Sink phase.dat (float). Fault: the connection reference -> Multiply Conjugate input 1 is deleted; GRC validation reports an unconnected port. Instruction: intended behaviour - phase.dat holds the phase of the test oscillator relative to the reference in radians, wrapped to (-pi, pi]; because the test oscillator runs 5 Hz fast, the phase rises steadily by 2 pi every 0.2 s (a sawtooth from -pi to pi), and the two oscillators must be kept as they are; symptom only (GRC refuses to generate: a port is not connected). Oracle: f2p corr_ref against the reference phase ramp in signed mode (tooling T2) so the inverted ramp (reference x conj(test)) fails; mean 0 (+-0.05), rms pi/sqrt3 = 1.814 (+-2 %), max_abs pi (+-1 %); p2p graph checks block_present analog_sig_source_x with freq 1000 and freq 1005 (params) and path from both sources to the File Sink via blocks_complex_to_arg (rules out a sawtooth source shortcut). Run length >= 1 s (5 periods), state R5. Variants: the restored connection; Multiply Conjugate inputs swapped with a Multiply Const -1 on the phase; Complex To Arg of each oscillator and a Subtract with wrap... only if it wraps identically (verify; otherwise drop). Mutants: inputs swapped (negated ramp), reference frequency 1.010 kHz (10 Hz ramp), Complex To Real instead of Arg, Complex To Mag, sink type complex (exclude equivalent mutants such as a changed oscillator amplitude, which Complex To Arg ignores). Block budget 5. Verified v2: mix|phase|tone -> test for both port orders (and for the arg-minus-arg alternative: combine|phase|tone, test). Training: t04_broken_sink_repair uses the same fault type (unconnected port); different graph and behaviour - record.

gbf-test-11.new_theme: MODIFY L1 (test) - add automatic gain control to a burst recording. Start graph (fs 48 kHz): a complex Signal Source 1 kHz amplitude 1 multiplied by a repeating Vector Source envelope (complex values: 0.05 for 4000 samples, then 1.5 for 4000 samples) -> File Sink rx.dat (complex), simulating weak and strong bursts. The user: 'add automatic gain control so that rx.dat has an RMS level of 1.0 (within 10 %) during both the weak and the strong parts, at most 1 ms after each level change, without changing the 1 kHz tone'. Oracle: rms checks on windows inside weak and strong parts after the stated settling time (several skip/n windows over >= 2 envelope periods), band_fraction around +1 kHz >= 0.99 (no distortion/shift), max_abs bound against overshoot if stated; p2p: the source chain unchanged (graph check block_present on the Signal Source params and the Vector Source) - a Multiply Const cannot equalise both levels, so no other shortcut. Variants: AGC (analog_agc_xx, rate chosen), AGC2 (attack/decay), feed-forward AGC, magnitude + moving average + Divide normaliser (data_source|divide|envelope|filter|mix, test) if it meets the settling spec. Mutants: AGC rate too slow (fails the 1 ms settling), reference 0.5, AGC bypassed, AGC before the multiplier (cannot level bursts), max_gain 10 (weak burst stays low). Block budget 5 (tone, envelope, multiply, AGC, sink). Verified v2: agc|data_source|mix -> test for both multiplier port orders; start graph data_source|mix. Training: t19_rssi_meter_build measures levels (no gain control) - record.

gbf-test-12.new_theme: PARAMETER-TUNE L1 (test) - set channel impairments to a stated carrier offset and SNR. Start graph (fs 48 kHz): complex Signal Source +3 kHz amplitude 0.5 -> Channel Model (noise_voltage 0, frequency_offset 0, epsilon 1.0, taps [1.0], fixed seed) -> File Sink rx.dat (complex). User: 'make the received test tone appear at +3.6 kHz (a 600 Hz carrier offset) with an SNR of 20 dB measured over the full 48 kHz bandwidth; change parameter values only and keep the transmitted tone, the timing offset and the single-path channel'. The model must convert to the Channel Model's normalised frequency offset 600/48000 = 0.0125 and to noise_voltage from the SNR (signal power 0.25 -> noise power 0.0025 -> noise_voltage 0.05; the fixer verifies the block's noise convention and states the SNR definition so it is unambiguous). Oracle: peak_freq 3600 +-1 %; band_fraction within +-50 Hz of 3.6 kHz = S/(S+N) with tolerance equivalent to +-1 dB SNR (and including the noise share inside that band); rms sqrt(0.2525) +-2 %; graph_checks same_blocks_as_start (+T1) p2p. Mutants: offset 600 entered in Hz (huge offset) or as 600/32000, SNR 10 dB / 30 dB, noise_voltage = 0.0025 (power instead of amplitude), epsilon changed, taps changed. Verified v2: channel_model|tone -> test (the rotator+noise alternative would be combine|mix|noise|tone, but tune tasks admit no structural alternatives). Training: t05_qam_debug (rates/types) is unrelated; none on channel impairments.

gbf-test-13.new_theme: BUILD L2 (test) - baseband-to-IF data transmitter. In the empty flowgraph: a repeating Vector Source of 32 NRZ symbols (+-1 floats listed in the instruction) at 4 kBd, interpolated by 8 to 32 kHz with a low-pass pulse-shaping filter (the instruction states the spectral requirement, not the design), converted to complex and shifted up to a +8 kHz complex IF; output if.dat (complex, 32 kHz). Requirements stated: at least 99 % of the power within +-3 kHz of +8 kHz, less than 0.5 % at negative frequencies, RMS within 5 % of the value implied by unit-amplitude symbols through a unity-DC-gain interpolation filter (fixer derives and calibrates across valid designs), and the transmitted symbol sequence carried by the signal: corr_ref of if.dat against the reference output (phase-invariant, min about 0.95, calibrated over the variants below so every valid pulse filter passes and a wrong symbol pattern fails). Run sentence R5. Use at least 6 functional blocks so the item is L2 under either reading (e.g. Vector Source, Repeat, Low Pass Filter, Float To Complex, Signal Source LO, Multiply, File Sink). Variants: Repeat + Low Pass Filter + Multiply by complex LO; Interpolating FIR with firdes.low_pass taps + Rotator; Rational Resampler + Rotator; RRC pulse shaping (data_source|mix|pulse_shaping|resample, test) if it meets the mask. Mutants: rectangular pulses (Repeat only: fails the mask), IF -8 kHz (sign), IF 6 kHz, interpolation 4 (wrong rate/bandwidth), real IF (Complex To Real: images at negative frequencies), symbols changed. Verified v2: data_source|filter|mix|resample -> test (interp FIR + rotator and repeat + LPF + multiply alike); a Constellation Modulator alternative would be data_source|linear_mod|mix|pulse_shaping|resample (train) - list it for the reserved list. Training: none on IF upconversion of data.

gbf-test-20.new_theme: PARAMETER-TUNE L2 (test) - retune a baseband PAM transmitter from 2-PAM to Gray-coded 4-PAM. Start graph (fs 48 kHz): repeating Vector Source of packed bytes (e.g. 8 bytes listed) -> Packed To Unpacked (bits_per_chunk 1, MSB first) -> Chunks To Symbols (float, table [-1, 1], dimension 1) -> Repeat (48: 1 kBd) -> File Sink pam.dat (float). User target: 4-PAM with Gray mapping, two bits per symbol taken MSB first, levels 00 -> -3, 01 -> -1, 11 -> +1, 10 -> +3, at 2.4 kBd, same data and output file; change parameter values only. The model must set bits_per_chunk 2, the table in index order [-3, -1, +3, +1] (index 0b10 = 2 -> +3, 0b11 = 3 -> +1), Repeat 20. Oracle: f2p equal_prefix exact on pam.dat from sample 0 over >= 2 data periods (max_offset 0); rms of the level sequence as a secondary check; graph_checks same_blocks_as_start (+T1) p2p. Mutants: natural (non-Gray) table [-3,-1,1,3], LSB-first, Repeat 24 (2 kBd), bits_per_chunk 1 with the 4-level table, levels scaled (+-1/+-3 swapped), table index order reversed. Verified v2: start and reference data_source|linear_mod|resample -> test. Training: t02_qpsk_ber_chain (QPSK modulator + BER) is the nearest linear-modulation spec; this is baseband 4-PAM symbol mapping with Gray coding - record.
